title: Scholia in Homeri Iliadem (A, bT, D): unit Book 6 / Scholia to the Iliad / Схолии к «Илиаде», песнь VI
author: Anonymous compilers. Sources: Aristonicus, Didymus, Herodian and Nicanor (the 'four-man commentary' in the A scholia), the exegetical tradition, Porphyry, and the Mythographus Homericus (D)
date: Hellenistic to late antique sources; Venetus A is 10th c.
genre: Scholia (textual criticism, grammar, literary criticism, mythography)
size: Erbse: 5 text vols, plus the D-scholia (van Thiel). Book 6 (A+bT+D): est. 15–20k words.
edition: Erbse 1969–88 (de Gruyter, in copyright). PD: Dindorf 1875–77 and Maass 1887–88. D-scholia: van Thiel 2014, open access (kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/5586).
ru_evidence: Russian search for scholia translations to the Iliad found none. Ru-wiki 'Схолии' says scholia are generally not translated into modern languages.
en_evidence: Beck et al., The Ancient Scholia to Homer's Iliad: A Translation, vol. 1 (Books 1–2), CUP 2025; further volumes pending. The D-scholia's mythological narratives only: Smith et al. 2023, CC BY (ToposText 866).
other_translations: None found for the full corpus.
value: The richest body of ancient literary and textual criticism, carrying the Alexandrian editors' readings. Indispensable for Homeric studies and the history of philology. The most emblematic text for a 'Neoscholia' platform.
ai_feasibility: Medium. Critical signs, Herodian's accentuation notes and Aristarchean terminology need a glossary, and source layers must stay labelled. The exegetical bT notes are easy. Base the work on the PD and open texts, since Erbse is in copyright.
pilot_unit: All scholia to Iliad 6 (Glaucus–Diomedes, Hector–Andromache); est. 15–20k words. Not yet covered by the CUP translation.
